title: About
text:
This project combines historical and real-time financial data with AI to produce automated research reports for US growth stock investors. By feeding macroeconomic indicators, equity market data, and commodity prices into an AI model, each report identifies historical patterns, draws parallels to current conditions, and highlights risks and opportunities for growth-oriented portfolios.
All charts and visualizations in the reports are created by the author — the AI generates only the written analysis.

Data Sources
Every report is grounded in real data from:

FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data): Inflation (CPI), GDP growth, unemployment, Fed balance sheet, Treasury yields, household debt, recession indicators, Fed funds rate, and high-yield credit spreads
Yahoo Finance: MSCI World Index, S&P 500, NASDAQ 100, Dow Jones, VIX, gold, and Brent crude oil
Multpl.com: S&P 500 trailing P/E ratios

title: Market Research
text:
Over the past three months leading up to July 24, 2026, global markets have presented a paradox of soaring asset prices and escalating geopolitical fragility. The MSCI World Index reached 4799.16 at the end of July 2026, driven largely by relentless momentum in US tech, while safe-haven gold surged to an unprecedented $4066.7 per ounce over the same period. Meanwhile, Brent crude spiked to $96.03 per barrel in late July 2026 amid the US-Iran conflict, echoing the supply-shock dynamics of the early 2020s. This bifurcation—record equities alongside record hard assets and rising energy-driven inflation—closely mirrors the late-stage exuberance of 1999 and the stagflationary whispers of 1978, forcing investors to weigh a productivity boom against severe macroeconomic tail risks.
The US equity market is flashing neon late-cycle signals. The S&P 500 closed at 7435.0 and the Nasdaq 100 at 28315.7 on 31 July 2026. The trailing P/E ratio of the S&P 500 sits at 28.49 at the end of July 2026, a valuation threshold we have only seen breached during the dot-com peak in 2000 and the post-pandemic liquidity frenzy of late 2021. Current 2026 consensus earnings growth is projected at a robust 25%, largely underwritten by AI infrastructure spending. However, this valuation expansion is occurring despite a deteriorating macroeconomic backdrop, creating a dangerous divergence between market pricing and economic reality.



Performance of Major US Stock Indices


Beneath the equity melt-up, the macroeconomic plumbing is showing stress. Unemployment drifted up to 4.2% by June 2026, while GDP growth moderated to 2.1% in Q1 2026. Headline CPI ticked back up to 3.2% in June 2026, heavily influenced by energy and geopolitical risk premiums. The Federal Reserve, having paused its easing cycle with the target rate sitting at 3.75% since December 2025, is effectively trapped. Furthermore, the Treasury yield curve has un-inverted, with the 10-year yield at 4.562% and the 2-year at 4.193% at the end of July 2026, resulting in a positive spread of roughly 37 basis points. Historically, the recession does not strike while the curve is inverted; it strikes shortly after the curve un-inverts, exactly as we saw prior to the 2001 and 2008 downturns.



US 2Y and 10Y Treasury Yields and Spread


Despite the Middle East escalation and the un-inverting yield curve, credit and volatility markets remain remarkably complacent. The ICE BofA High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread compressed to 2.77% in July 2026, signaling zero perceived credit stress, while the VIX languished at 17.91 in late July 2026. This complacency is puzzling given that gold has more than doubled since 2023 to $4066.7 in July 2026, and Brent oil sits at $96.03. The bond and equity markets are pricing in a soft landing powered by AI, while the commodities markets are pricing in a structural breakdown of global supply chains and fiat currency debasement.



Gold Prices


When mapping this data against historical boom and bust cycles, specific risks and opportunities emerge for the growth investor:

Risk: The “Un-inversion” Recession Trap. The current 10Y/2Y spread of +37 bps mirrors the exact macroeconomic sequencing of mid-2000 and mid-2007. If AI earnings fail to materialize broadly across the broader economy, the lagged effects of previous tightening combined with rising unemployment could trigger a violent multiple compression in long-duration assets.
Risk: Geopolitical Stagflation. The US-Iran conflict and Houthi disruptions in the Red Sea have pushed Brent to $96.03. If this becomes a prolonged supply shock rather than a temporary disruption, it will reignite inflation well above the 3.2% June 2026 print, forcing the Fed into a corner where it cannot cut rates to support the equity market.
Opportunity: AI Monetization Monopolies. With S&P 500 earnings expected to grow 25% in 2026, the opportunity lies in the narrow bandwidth of companies actually building and monetizing the AI physical layer. These are the only assets justifying a 28.5x P/E in a slowing economy, as they possess the pricing power to pass through higher energy costs.
Opportunity: Hard Assets and Debasement Hedges. Gold’s relentless march to $4066.7 and the structural bid in energy assets present a clear opportunity to portfolio-hedge against the fiscal dominance and debt monetization that the US household debt service ratio of 11.16% in Q1 2026 implies.




MSCI World Equity Index


Given the extreme valuations, the historical precedent of the yield curve un-inversion, and the escalating geopolitical risks in the Middle East, the risk-reward for broad market growth indices is highly unfavorable. However, the secular AI boom provides a unique earnings tailwind that defies traditional late-cycle gravity. Therefore, a 25-50% portfolio exposure to US growth stocks is recommended. This defensive posture allows for participation in the AI infrastructure winners while maintaining sufficient cash and commodity hedges to survive a potential late-cycle earnings recession and geopolitical shock.
